who: Anyone who has not been diagnosed yet
takeaways: Nothing on the page flashes more than three times in any one second, unless the flashes are below the general flash and red flash thresholds.
Flashing can trigger seizures. The harm can be immediate and serious, so this is Level A.
A flash is a quick change from light to dark and back. Saturated red flashing is treated more strictly.
It covers everything on the page, including videos, ads and animations you did not make yourself.
failures: A strobing “breaking news” or sale banner
A video with lightning, gunfire or camera flashes
A rapid light-dark flicker used as an error or alert effect
check: Count the flashes in each animation. More than three in any one second needs attention.
Run videos and complex animations through a flash analysis tool before release.
Check third-party content such as ads and embedded video, not only your own work.

quiz.question: A game’s win screen flashes the whole background between white and black five times a second for two seconds. What should you do?
options: Keep it, and add a warning before it plays
Keep it, but let people turn it off in settings
Change it to three flashes a second or fewer, or a non-flashing effect
quiz.why: A large, high-contrast flash at five per second is the exact pattern this rule forbids. A warning or an off switch does not help someone who has a seizure before they can react.

spec: Give the timing of every flashing or blinking effect, in flashes per second.
Mark any video or animation that needs a flash analysis before it ships.
Specify a slower or non-flashing version for any effect that came close.
review: Is there anything here that flickers or strobes?
Who checks the videos and ads we did not design?
Could this alert get attention without flashing at all?
tradeoff: Flashing grabs attention, which is why people reach for it. Use color, size or a single pulse instead. They get attention without the risk.
system: Set motion tokens so no blink or pulse can run faster than three times a second, and forbid full-screen flashing in the guidelines.
pitch: This is the one rule where getting it wrong can put someone in hospital. It costs us nothing to avoid.
